text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementHealthWhy Sleep Might Not be as Restorative as We Get OlderOur brains need a nightly scrubbing JCBy Jake Currie4:00 PM CST on November 13, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleEvery night, you get brainwashed. Powered By 1071.4K 10ShareNextStayAs you’re sleeping, slow brain waves trigger gentle pulses of cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) that bathe your brain, flushing out the waste that’s accumulated during the day. It’s an important process, and one that’s been linked to cognitive health, neuroprotection, and memory consolidation. Of course, as we age, we also tend to sleep less. Now, a new study published in Nature Aging is taking a look at what happens to these revitalizing waves as we get older.  A team of neuroscientists led by imaging specialists at the Massachusetts Institute of Technology recruited some young (ages 18-39) and older (ages 60-84) volunteers to spend a night getting their brains scanned. While they dozed, the participants had their noggins imaged by both fMRI and a modified MRI technique to measure CSF flow. Their brain activity was also recorded by an EEG machine. As the younger group drifted off, their slow EEG waves intensified—and the CSF pulses followed suit. Among the older participants, however, these CSF waves were markedly weaker.  Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
